A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FaRMA, with matching authors, algorithms, theoretical results and benchmarks. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations on TL;DR, Anthropic HH and Ultra-Feedback, including rewards, generation times, diversity, GPT-4 judgments and training costs.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds smaller-model results, additional comparator results, a beta ablation and a training-time/memory comparison.

M1.justification: The vocabulary-wide reward outputs, alternating Bradley-Terry and maximum-consistency losses, and decoding procedure remain unchanged. Algorithms 1 and 2 are retained; the smaller models are evaluation configurations of the existing method.

E1.justification: Both versions train and evaluate on TL;DR summarization, Anthropic HH dialogue and Ultra-Feedback text generation. The additions use these existing datasets and tasks without introducing a distinct data domain or test scenario.

E2.justification: Table 4 adds CD and PARGS to the diversity comparisons on both TL;DR and HH. Appendix A, Table 5 adds PARGS to the Ultra-Feedback comparison. These are comparator additions within existing experiments, although the methods already appeared elsewhere in v1.

E3.justification: Table 3 replaces the reported 1.4B half-size reward-model setting with 1B and 400M settings. v2 also introduces a single-A100 training-cost comparison using Llama 3.2-1B, measures peak memory, and sweeps beta over 0.5, 1.0, 1.5 and 2.0. Existing benchmark sample counts and evaluation procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix D tests sensitivity to beta through a four-value sweep, and Table 3 extends the existing reward-model-size analysis down to 400M parameters. The CARDS threshold analysis and generated examples are retained under renumbered appendices.

E5.justification: Both versions report benchmark reward means with standard errors. Additional result rows and the beta sweep use existing uncertainty-reporting conventions; no new seed counts, repeated-run procedures, confidence intervals or significance tests are documented.

E6.justification: Core benchmark results remain stable, but several supporting results are added or replaced. Table 3 replaces the 1.4B result of 1.41 ± 0.16 with 1B and 400M results of 1.56 ± 0.18 and 1.49 ± 0.12; these are different settings. Added PARGS scores highest on Ultra-Feedback at -1.01 ± 0.26 versus FaRMA's retained -1.20 ± 0.21. Tables 10–11 add training-cost and beta-sweep results, and Table 4 adds diversity scores.

T1.justification: Theorems 1–3, their assumptions and proofs, the maximum-consistency constraint and the Bellman derivation are retained. Equation renumbering, explicit conditioning on x and corrected mathematical typesetting do not change the reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: simultaneous next-token scoring, a constraint favoring optimal extensions, faster inference and competitive alignment. Added experiments support these existing claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: Section 6.2 extends the practical interpretation of smaller reward models to 400M parameters. New Appendix D states that changing beta does not affect inference time. Section 3.2 refines its criticism of reference-policy-dependent value learning into an argument about possible bias.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code repository link in the abstract and documents the hardware, training times and peak memory for the additional single-A100 comparison. Existing software versions and training hyperparameter tables in Appendix B are retained.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds a paragraph on stepwise value functions in adversarial text generation, citing Li et al. (2017), Tuan et al. (2018), and Tuan and Lee (2019). It distinguishes their generator training through reinforcement learning from reward-guided decoding. Other reference changes largely update metadata or consolidate a duplicate citation.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized grammar, terminology and cross-reference corrections, renames Section 4 to 'FaRMA: Cost-Effective RGTG', and adds acknowledgments and a hyperparameter-ablation appendix. The main narrative and section order remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 10–11, expands Tables 3–5 and relocates Table 1 through page reflow. Figures 1–2 retain their graphical content, with minor caption editing. Existing appendix tables and example boxes are preserved.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens validation through a common-hardware training-cost comparison, beta sensitivity results and additional comparators, while adding code-access information. Table 10 makes the efficiency evidence easier to interpret than v1's mixed-hardware Table 9. The gains are limited by a new inconsistency: Appendix A retains its best-reward statement although added PARGS has a higher mean reward than FaRMA. Overall, the additions modestly improve an otherwise stable paper.
